goal: Enforce standard run ID, Issue, and spec target guards for preparing-flow prelude commands before mutation, agent execution, or worktree creation while preserving existing routing and guard-free behavior.

in: Expose the selected preparing run as `preparingFlowState` while retaining `flowState: null` in preparing-mode context.
Validate target guards against `preparingFlowState ?? flowState` in the base command and dispatcher before command or lifecycle side effects.
Align request, note, auto, auto-check, and prepare preparing-mode routing, registry guard options, and help text.
Keep explicit unknown run IDs isolated from unrelated active or preparing flows.
Add focused existing and spec-local tests for selection, matching and mismatching guards, side-effect ordering, help parity, and post-prepare behavior.
out: FlowStore, PreparingFlowStore, flow set init, and flow get status behavior changes.
New public commands, broader target semantics, manual state recovery, or compatibility paths.
Issue 415 or any other flow, worktree, feature implementation, or recovery.
External dependencies, push, publish, or release.

constraints: Use only Node.js built-in modules and existing command, registry, envelope, and class patterns.
Retain `flowState: null` for preparing-mode routing and expose selected preparing state only through `preparingFlowState`.
Do not change FlowStore ownership, preparing-state storage, init semantics, or status semantics.
Reject guard mismatches as `ACTIVE_FLOW_MISMATCH` before mutation, command module loading, agent execution, lifecycle hooks, or worktree creation.
Preserve documented behavior when no target guard is supplied, including existing command-specific failures for a guard-free unknown `--run-id`.
design_principles: Represent the selected preparing target explicitly instead of changing the meaning of active flow state.
Apply one shared target-state selection rule at both command and dispatcher safety boundaries.
Make explicit run selection authoritative, including a missing-run result, so it cannot fall through.
Keep registry argument metadata and rendered help synchronized through existing target-option helpers.

modules.text: `src/flow/lib/flow-context.js` selects active or preparing authority and exposes the selected preparing state without changing preparing routing state.
`src/flow/lib/base-command.js` performs command-level target validation against the selected active or preparing state.
`src/lib/dispatcher.js` rejects target mismatches before command loading, lifecycle hooks, execution, and worktree or agent side effects.
`src/flow/registry.js` owns prelude command routing declarations, accepted guard options, and help parity.

data_flow.text: An explicit `--run-id` selects exactly one preparing record; the context retains `flowState: null` and publishes the selected record as `preparingFlowState`, or an isolated empty preparing target snapshot when that explicit run does not exist.
The dispatcher and FlowCommand choose `preparingFlowState ?? flowState`, compare all supplied expectations, and return `ACTIVE_FLOW_MISMATCH` before any side effect when one differs.

After successful validation, request, note, auto, auto-check, or prepare follows its existing preparing route; prepare promotes the same run to flow.json and subsequent guards validate the active state.

decisions.text: [CORRECTION] checked preparing selection in `src/flow/lib/flow-context.js`; retain `flowState: null`, expose the loaded state as `preparingFlowState`, and isolate an explicit missing run instead of continuing to active discovery.
decisions.evidence: `preparingAuthorityForRunId()` currently discards the loaded state and returns only `flowState: null`; when it returns null for an unknown run, `resolveAuthorityFlowState()` proceeds to active-flow resolution.

decisions.text: [CORRECTION] checked null-state guard behavior; represent an explicit missing preparing run with an isolated empty target snapshot so supplied expectations mismatch within the approved files, while guard-free calls continue to command-owned missing-run errors.
decisions.evidence: `targetMismatchEnvelopeForInput()` does not report a mismatch for null state and `src/lib/flow-target-guard.js` is out of scope; a non-null empty snapshot activates existing comparisons without changing guard-free paths.

decisions.text: [CORRECTION] checked shared command validation in `src/flow/lib/base-command.js`; validate the selected target state while keeping `requiresFlow` based on active routing state.
decisions.evidence: `FlowCommand.run()` currently passes only `ctx.flowState` to `targetMismatchEnvelopeForInput`, so requiresFlow:false preparing commands parse expectations but do not validate them.

decisions.text: [CORRECTION] checked dispatcher ordering in `src/lib/dispatcher.js`; use selected preparing state for guard validation and runtime target identity before command loading, hooks, execution, or side effects.
decisions.evidence: `dispatch()` builds hook context and validates only `hookCtx.flowState` at step 3, before module loading and hooks; extending that target selection preserves the existing early-return boundary.

decisions.text: [CORRECTION] checked registry parity; add standard guard options/help to auto-check and prepare, and declare note as `requiresFlow:false` so its existing dual-mode command can reach preparing routing.
decisions.evidence: `prepare.args` and `run.auto-check.args` omit `FLOW_TARGET_GUARD_OPTIONS`; request and auto declare `requiresFlow:false`, but note does not even though `SetNoteCommand` itself uses `super({ requiresFlow:false })`.

decisions.text: [VERIFY] checked request, note, and auto implementations; result=match: each already uses explicit preparing run resolution and mutates the selected preparing record after command entry.
decisions.evidence: `set-request.js`, `set-note.js`, and `set-auto.js` call `resolvePreparingRunId()` and then `mutatePreparingFlow()` when `flowState` is null.

decisions.text: Migration parity inventory maps guard-free request/note/auto behavior to existing command owners, null preparing routing and unknown-run isolation to flow-context, shared guard rejection to base-command/dispatcher, auto-check/prepare options and help to registry, and post-prepare guard validation to existing active-state paths; no public behavior is removed.
decisions.evidence: Issue 431 Requirements and Verification explicitly require guard-free compatibility, selection shape, all five command surfaces, unknown-run isolation, pre-side-effect rejection, help parity, and post-prepare guards.

background: Prelude commands operate before flow.json exists and therefore route through a preparing record. The current context intentionally reports no active flow for that route, but shared guards inspect only active flow state. As a result, request, note, and auto accept expectations without enforcing them, while auto-check and prepare do not accept the standard options. A missing explicit run can also continue into unrelated active-flow discovery. The repair must make the selected preparing identity available to shared guard boundaries without converting it into an active flow or changing storage ownership.

requirements.desc: Preparing selection shall return both `flowState: null` and the loaded `preparingFlowState`; when an explicit non-empty run ID does not exist, selection shall return `flowState: null` plus an isolated empty `preparingFlowState` snapshot and shall not fall through to unrelated active or preparing flow discovery.

FlowCommand and dispatcher target validation shall evaluate `preparingFlowState ?? flowState` for `--expect-run-id`, `--expect-issue`, and `--expect-spec`, returning `ACTIVE_FLOW_MISMATCH` before mutation, command module execution, lifecycle hooks, agent calls, runtime target persistence, or worktree creation while preserving existing `requiresFlow` routing semantics.

`flow set request`, `flow set note`, and `flow set auto` shall use coherent preparing routing with matching guards succeeding, each guard mismatch failing before mutation, a non-null expected spec failing while preparing spec is null, guarded explicit unknown runs returning `ACTIVE_FLOW_MISMATCH`, and guard-free documented behavior including unknown-run errors unchanged; registry note routing shall declare `requiresFlow:false` consistently with its command class.

`flow run auto-check` and `flow prepare` shall accept and document the standard run ID, Issue, and spec guard options using registry helper conventions; guarded mismatches and guarded unknown runs shall return `ACTIVE_FLOW_MISMATCH` before auto-check agent execution or prepare branch/worktree/spec creation, guard-free unknown runs shall retain command-specific failures, and matching guarded prepare shall return the promoted spec.

After successful prepare, matching run ID, Issue, and spec guards shall continue to succeed against the active flow, changing any one shall return `ACTIVE_FLOW_MISMATCH`, and all existing guard-free public behavior and FlowStore ownership shall remain unchanged.

Focused unit, end-to-end, and spec-local tests shall pair every retained behavior with evidence: selection shape; request/note/auto guard-free and guarded routes; all mismatch types; unknown-run no-fallback; auto-check no-agent rejection; prepare no-worktree rejection; successful guarded prepare; post-prepare three-guard behavior; and registry/help parity.

acceptance_criteria: AC1: A flow-context unit test selects a known preparing run and observes `flowState === null`, `preparingFlowState` with the expected run and Issue, main authority root, and no active-flow discovery.

AC2: An explicit unknown run ID with unrelated active or preparing flows present produces an isolated empty `preparingFlowState`, does not select either unrelated flow, returns `ACTIVE_FLOW_MISMATCH` when any expectation guard is supplied, and retains the existing command-specific error when invoked without guards.

AC3: Preparing request, note, and auto calls with matching run and Issue guards succeed; changing run, Issue, or expected spec returns `ACTIVE_FLOW_MISMATCH` before the preparing state changes; guard-free calls retain documented results.
AC4: Registry and help tests show the same standard target guard definitions for request, note, auto, auto-check, and prepare, with note routed as a requiresFlow:false dual-mode command.

AC5: Auto-check with matching preparing guards reaches its existing execution path; each mismatch and an unknown run with supplied expectation guards return `ACTIVE_FLOW_MISMATCH` without invoking the agent or persisting an auto-check verdict, while guard-free unknown-run behavior remains unchanged.

AC6: Prepare with matching run and Issue guards succeeds and returns a spec; each mismatch, a non-null expected spec while preparing spec is null, and an unknown run with supplied expectation guards return `ACTIVE_FLOW_MISMATCH` before branch, worktree, spec directory, or hook creation, while guard-free unknown-run behavior remains unchanged.
AC7: After prepare, matching run, Issue, and returned spec guards succeed, while changing any one returns `ACTIVE_FLOW_MISMATCH`; guard-free continuation remains unchanged.
AC8: Spec-local tests include `// spec: R<N>` coverage for R1-R6, focused existing suites pass, and the configured targeted and final project regressions pass without harness files entering Git.

alternatives_considered.reason: Rejected because shared base-command and dispatcher boundaries already own target validation ordering and prevent duplication across command surfaces.

alternatives_considered.reason: Rejected because explicit caller intent must remain isolated and the Issue requires no unrelated-flow fallback.
Rejected because existing stores already provide the required state and are explicitly out of scope.
